item.question: A Category I AIF has a total corpus of Rs 300 crore. What is the minimum continuing interest the Manager or Sponsor must maintain in this fund under SEBI AIF Regulations, 2012?

result.answer: According to Securities and exchange board of india alternative inve (in force since 2012-01-01): "Regulation 10(d): the Manager or Sponsor shall have a continuing interest in the Alternative Investment Fund of not less than two and half percent of the corpus or five crore rupees, whichever is lower, in the form of investment in the Alternative Investment Fund and such interest shall not be through the waiver of management fees: Provided that for Category III Alternative Investment Fund, the continuing interest shall be not less than five percent of the corpus or ten crore rupees, whichever is lower."

item.question: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018, what fraction of the anchor investor portion in a book-built issue is reserved for domestic mutual funds?

result.answer: According to Securities and exchange board of india issue of capital (in force since 2018-01-01): "One-third of the anchor investor portion shall be reserved for domestic mutual funds."

item.question: What restriction does SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 impose on the Chairman of an asset management company?

result.answer: According to Securities and exchange board of india mutual funds reg (in force since 1996-01-01): "The original Regulation 47 of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations required: 'Every mutual fund shall ensure that the asset management company computes and carries out valuation of investments made by its scheme(s) in accordance with the investment valuation norms specified in the Eighth Schedule.' This obligation was subsequently moved to Regulation 25(19) and Regulation 47 was substituted by the SEBI (Mutual Funds) (Amendment) Regulations, 2023."

item.question: What six categories of client information must an investment adviser obtain from a client for the purpose of risk profiling under SEBI IA Regulations, 2013?

result.answer: According to Securities and exchange board of india investment advis (in force since 2013-01-01): "Regulation 16(a): it obtains from the client, such information as is necessary for the purpose of giving investment advice, including the following: (i) age; (ii) investment objectives including time for which they wish to stay invested, the purposes of the investment; (iii) income details; (iv) existing investments/assets; (v) risk appetite/tolerance; (vi) liability/borrowing details."

item.question: How must a credit rating agency disseminate information about newly assigned ratings and rating changes under SEBI (CRA) Regulations, 1999? What additional step is required for listed company securities?

result.answer: According to Securities and exchange board of india credit rating ag (in force since 1999-01-01): "Regulation 15(2): Every credit rating agency shall disseminate information regarding newly assigned ratings, and changes in earlier rating promptly through press releases and websites, and, in the case of securities issued by listed companies, such information shall also be provided simultaneously to the concerned regional stock exchange and to all the stock exchanges where the said securities are listed."

item.question: Under Regulation 5(2) of SEBI Takeovers Regulations 2011, under what condition is an indirect acquisition treated as a direct acquisition for all purposes of the regulations?

result.answer: According to Securities and exchange board of india substantial acqu (in force since 2011-01-01): "Regulation 5(2): In case of an indirect acquisition where (a) the proportionate net asset value of the target company as a percentage of the consolidated NAV, (b) the proportionate sales turnover as a percentage of consolidated sales turnover, or (c) the proportionate market capitalisation as a percentage of enterprise value of the entity being acquired is in excess of eighty per cent, such indirect acquisition shall be regarded as a direct acquisition for all purposes including timing, pricing and compliance requirements."
